D019-D016_h001.question:
I’ve been having a hard time sleeping—night after night, I wake up from the same kind of dream. It’s not always clear, but there’s fire, chaos, people shouting… and I’m just standing there, unable to move or help. I don’t know exactly where it’s from—maybe something I saw on the news a while back, or a memory I can’t quite place. It just keeps coming back, even when I’m awake.

During the day, these fragments pop into my head uninvited—a flash of smoke, a face I don’t recognize, the sound of an alarm. I try to push them away, refocus on the weather models, but they linger, like static between signals. I’ve started checking the morning forecast three or four times before the briefing, not because I think it’s wrong, but because I need to be certain. My wife noticed—I used to be able to let things go. Now, I feel like I’m always bracing for something, like there’s a storm building I can’t predict.

It’s been about a month. I thought I’d shake it, but instead it just feels heavier, like I’m replaying something I didn’t survive fully.
D019-D016_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D019-D016_h001.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h002.question:
I’ve just turned 31, and for the past few weeks—since that last big call I was on—I haven’t felt like myself. I’m home every night, back with my wife, but I can’t seem to settle. I sleep, but I wake up just as tired as when I went to bed. Doesn’t matter how long I’m out; it’s like my body never shuts off.

There are certain things—smells, sounds, even the way the light hits the fire station in the afternoon—that set something off inside me. My chest tightens, my heart races. It’s like I’m back there, but I don’t know *where* “there” fully is, if that makes sense. I can’t quite piece it all together. There are thoughts, sure—some things loop in my head, over and over—flashes of smoke, voices, maybe something I missed. But they don’t feel like rituals or anything I’m trying to control. I’m not doing anything different, not repeating actions or washing my hands or that kind of thing.

I keep wondering if I’m overreacting. I’ve seen tough stuff before. But this time, something’s stuck—and I don’t know if it’s the job, my head, or just needing more time.
D019-D016_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D019-D016_h002.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h003.question:
I’ve been having a real hard time sleeping lately—night after night, I wake up sweating, heart pounding, from dreams that feel too real. I’m out in the fields, same as always, but something goes wrong... animals acting strange, fences down, or worse—something happens to my wife. I can't shake it when I wake up. It’s been going on for a few weeks now, ever since that storm blew through and the barn caught fire. I got everyone out safe, thank God, but I keep seeing it in my sleep.

During the day, those images just pop into my head—flames, smoke, the sound of the roof caving in. I know it’s over, but it feels like it’s happening all over again. I check the smoke detectors three times before bed. Not because I want to, but if I don’t, my chest tightens and I can’t sit still. I walk the property every evening, making sure every outlet’s off, every gate latched. My wife says I’m worrying too much, but I can’t help it—what if I missed something?

Truth is, I don’t know if it’s the fire messing with my head, or if I’m just getting too old for this. I just want to sleep through the night without seeing that damn barn go up in flames again.
D019-D016_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D019-D016_h003.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h004.question:
I’ve been having these nightmares—almost every night now. I’m back in the school, but it’s empty, completely silent, and suddenly the lights go out. I can’t move, can’t call out. I wake up shaky, like I’m still there. I’ve started dreading bedtime.  

During the day, certain things catch me off guard—a flickering light, the sound of a door closing too hard—and my chest just tightens. I have to step away, take deep breaths. It’s not like I can’t function, but everything feels… closer, sharper. I’ll be teaching my students and then suddenly I’m not present anymore.  

And there’s this thought that keeps coming—what if I left the stove on at home? I know I turned it off, I checked three times this morning before school, but later, I’m still wondering. I replay it in my head. Did I really turn it off? No harm’s come from it—I haven’t gone back or done anything out of the way. It just… won’t leave.  

It’s been about three weeks since the incident at school, that lockdown drill that went wrong. I thought I was okay, but now I’m not so sure. I’m managing, but everything feels a little fragile.
D019-D016_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D019-D016_h004.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h005.question:
I’ve been having a rough time sleeping lately—waking up two, three times a night, and once I’m up, my mind just races. It’s been going on for about three weeks now. I keep remembering this accident I saw while I was out on my route... a bad car crash near the school. I didn’t even stop because I thought someone else would help, but now I can’t shake it. I see the twisted metal, the broken glass… it just pops up when I’m sorting mail, when I’m eating dinner, even in the middle of talking to my wife.  

These thoughts aren’t like worries—I don’t feel like I have to do anything to fix them, but they come over and over, sharp and sudden. I keep wondering if I should’ve done more. I haven’t been avoiding the area—I still walk that route—but it hits me harder each time. My wife says I’ve been quieter, more withdrawn, but there’s no pattern to it. I don’t have any rituals or things I need to repeat, and it’s not like I’m anxious all the time. Just these flashes. I don’t know if it’s stress or just guilt or what.
D019-D016_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Delusional Disorder
D019-D016_h005.answer: C & B. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h006.question:
Lately, I just feel... hollow. It’s like there’s a fog between me and everything else—my kids, my work, even things I used to love. I can’t sleep through the night. I keep having these dreams—vivid, awful ones—where I’m back *there*, in that moment, but it’s never clear what happens. I wake up sweating and can’t get back to sleep. Funny thing is, I can remember pieces of what happened—the lighting, the sound of the intercom—but huge chunks are just... gone. Like my mind blacked them out on purpose.

Since it happened, I’ve been stuck in a loop. These thoughts just crash in—unwanted, sharp, like a record skipping. I don’t know where they come from, but they repeat, over and over, even when I’m charting at work or washing dishes. I *try* not to react—I’m a nurse, I deal with trauma every day—but now it feels like I don’t feel anything at all. My ex said I’ve changed, that I’m distant. Maybe he’s right. I just don’t know how to reset, or even if this is something that will pass. It’s been a few weeks. Not sure if it’s grief, stress, or something else entirely.
D019-D016_h006.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D016_h006.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h007.question:
I’ve been… off… for about three weeks now. Ever since that night—the accident—I can’t seem to shake this fog. I wake up in the middle of the night, heart racing, drenched in sweat. The dream is always fragmented: headlights, glass shattering, but I can’t piece together what exactly happened. I know I walked away, but I keep thinking I should remember more than I do. My husband says I’ve been distant, that I don’t react when he tells me good things—like when I won the case last week, something I’d normally be proud of. I just nodded. It felt hollow, like I was watching someone else live my life.

There are these thoughts—constant, looping—they come out of nowhere. Did I cause it? Could I have stopped it? Even when I’m in a meeting, reviewing contracts, they intrude. I don’t do anything to stop them, no rituals or routines, but they won’t leave. I don’t want to tell my team I’m struggling. I’m supposed to be sharp, in control. But I’m neither. I can’t recall the whole night, and maybe that’s the worst part—not knowing what I’ve lost.
D019-D016_h007.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D016_h007.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h008.question:
I’ve just turned 45, and honestly, it’s been hard to feel anything much at all lately—not joy, not relief, not even pride when my son graduated last month. I kept waiting to feel happy for him, but it was like watching life through a fogged window. I work nights on the psych ward, so sleep’s never perfect, but now I’m waking up gasping—same dream almost every night: blood on the floor, voices I can’t place, shadows moving. I don’t know what it’s about. It feels real, but I can’t pin down where it happened or why it shakes me so much.

There are gaps in my memory from… something. I remember helping with a crisis last winter—an agitated patient, codes called—but what came after? Nothing solid. And that bothers me, especially since I’m supposed to be sharp, attentive. Now I catch myself going over the same thoughts again and again, like a record stuck—Did I miss a sign? Did I contribute? They’re not always about the job, though. Sometimes it’s just… numbers, or door handles, or whether I locked my car—nothing drastic, but they linger.

I don’t do anything special about them—no checking, no rituals—but I can’t seem to turn the noise off. It’s just there, humming under everything.
D019-D016_h008.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D016_h008.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h009.question:
I’ve been having trouble sleeping for about three weeks now—waking up two, sometimes three times a night, and once I’m up, I can’t seem to settle. It started not long after we had that rough storm off the coast. Nothing we couldn’t handle, but something about it… it just stuck with me. I don’t remember much from those few hours—whole chunks are just gone, which worries me. A captain should remember his watch.  

Even when things are calm, when my wife sends a kind message or the crew laughs over dinner, I don’t feel it—the warmth, the joy. It’s like I’m watching it from the other side of glass. And my mind keeps circling the same thoughts: *Did I give the right order? Was the rudder response slow? Should we have turned earlier?* They play over and over, but I wouldn’t call them fears I need to fix with rituals or actions. I don’t check the compass six times or repeat phrases—no, it’s not that. They’re just… there. Lingering. I can still work, still command, but something’s off—like I’m foggy, disconnected, and those thoughts won’t drop anchor.
D019-D016_h009.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D016_h009.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h010.question:
I’ve been off since the building collapse last month—three weeks now. I keep having the same dream over and over: twisted steel, voices under rubble, but I can’t see faces. I wake up drenched, heart slamming, like I’m still trapped. But when I try to remember what happened during the rescue… it’s like a fog. I know we pulled people out, but whole chunks—gone. I can’t piece it together.

The worst part is, nothing feels right anymore. My daughter drew me a picture at breakfast, beaming, and I just… couldn’t feel it. I smiled, I said thank you, but inside? Flat. No joy, no warmth—just emptiness where that should be.

And then there are these thoughts… not about the collapse, not exactly. Just these looping bits—like did I lock the rig, did I miss a breath sound, did I leave someone behind even though I know checks were done. They pop up at random, not during routines, and I don’t do anything to fix them—no checking, no rituals—just… sit with them. My wife says I’m distant. I just don’t know how to explain that part.
D019-D016_h010.options:
A. Specific Phobia
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D019-D016_h010.answer: D & C. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge for the past few weeks—maybe longer. It’s like I can’t ever settle down, even at home when I’m supposed to be relaxed. I’ll sit on the couch and feel this tightness in my chest, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen. My husband’s noticed—I can tell he’s worried. I keep jumping when he walks into the room, even if he’s quiet. Sudden movements, like someone waving a hand or standing up fast, make me flinch hard.

The strangest part is making decisions. As an accountant, I’ve always prided myself on being organized, but now I can’t even pick what to wear in the morning. I’ll stand in front of the closet, second-guessing myself: “Is this too warm? Too formal?” It takes me ten minutes just to choose a shirt. Same with meals. I’ll read the menu over and over and still feel stuck.

And my mind… it keeps circling back to certain thoughts. Not memories, exactly—just ideas that pop up, like things going wrong at work or something happening to my family. I don’t act on them, but I can’t shake them either. I just sit with the worry, waiting for the next thing that might go wrong.
D019-D016_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D019-D016_h011.answer: C & D. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h012.question:
I’ve been off since that night a few weeks ago—can’t really say exactly what happened, but it involved a fight outside the gym after a class. Since then, it’s like my brain won’t shut off. I’ll be talking to someone and suddenly lose track of the conversation, like my mind just blanks. It’s messing with my coaching—I hate having to ask clients to repeat themselves. 

I keep checking the doors, windows, anyone coming in or out. If someone walks in fast or comes up behind me, I jump—like, full body flinch. It’s embarrassing, especially when it happens in the middle of a session. I’ve been noticing every little movement in the room now, can’t help it. 

And then there’s the thoughts. They just show up—like, “What if I hurt someone by accident?” or “What if I left the door unlocked and someone gets in?” They don’t feel like mine, and they don’t go away easily. I don’t do anything to fix them, no rituals or anything, but they linger. It’s not like I’m scared because of something that happened before—it’s just… there. Can’t say it’s been long enough to know if it’ll go away, but it’s starting to wear me down.
D019-D016_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D019-D016_h012.answer: C & D. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling on edge for about a month now—ever since my last patient passed so suddenly. It wasn’t unexpected, medically, but something about how it happened… I keep replaying it. Not vivid images, exactly, but thoughts that circle, like I’m trying to catch something I missed. I can’t focus long enough to read a book or even track where I left my coffee cup. I swear I had it two seconds ago—did I leave it in the staff room?

I can’t seem to relax, even at home. My body feels tight all the time, like I’m waiting for something bad to happen. The other day, a car backfired outside and I jumped so hard I dropped my keys—same thing when the door slams at work. My coworker startled me with a cough once, and I flinched like I’d been hit.

The thoughts don’t come with rituals or anything—I don’t do anything to “fix” them. They just show up: “Did I do enough? Was there a sign I ignored?” But they’re not tied to any one event, really. Just… constant. I can’t shut them off, but I don’t act on them. I just feel tired—mentally worn out.
D019-D016_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D019-D016_h013.answer: C & D. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h014.question:
I’ve been struggling to feel like myself for about a month now—ever since that storm chase went sideways. I wasn’t hurt, not really, but something about it stuck with me. Lately, I can’t decide anything without overthinking. Picking what to wear, what to eat—it all feels overwhelming. I stand in front of the closet and freeze, like each choice has some hidden consequence.

At work, I keep scanning the radar, sure. That’s part of the job. But now I catch myself scanning the room, too—doors, windows, exits. If a car backfires or a cup drops, I flinch hard, sometimes even jump out of my chair. My wife says I’m “on edge all the time,” and she’s not wrong.

There are thoughts, too—bits of images, sounds—that just pop up: wind tearing at the vehicle, the radio crackling unintelligibly. I don’t know if they’re about that day or just random. I don’t do anything to stop them—no routines or checks—but I can’t seem to shut them off. They’re just… there. I keep waiting to snap out of it, but I haven’t.
D019-D016_h014.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D019-D016_h014.answer: C & D. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h015.question:
I’ve been struggling for the past few weeks—maybe a little over a month—since that incident out in Wyoming, when I swerved off the shoulder to avoid hitting a deer and nearly rolled the truck. Nothing broken, just scrapes, but something’s been off ever since. My head feels… foggy, like I can’t quite get my thoughts together, especially during long stretches on the highway. I keep replaying the moment, but not just that—I also catch myself stuck on these weird mental loops, like wondering if I left the garage door open back home, even though I know my ex took care of the house.

I’m always watching now—side mirrors, rearview, scanning the shoulders, the oncoming headlights. If someone cuts me off, I jump hard, heart racing like I’ve seen a ghost. Same if a pedestrian just pops up near a rest area. I can’t relax. I keep turning the radio off because sudden sounds make me flinch. I don’t know if it’s about the crash anymore or just… everything in my head feels stuck on repeat. But I don’t do anything different—no checking rituals or anything like that. Just the thoughts.
D019-D016_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Acute Stress Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D019-D016_h015.answer: C & D. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h016.question:
I’ve been having these moments—snapshots, really—where I’m back there, in the compound. Just yesterday, the sound of a helicopter overhead made me drop my coffee cup because I was suddenly sure I was in the motor pool during the attack. I can't remember much from that day, whole chunks are just... gone. My sergeant tried talking to me about it later, but I shut him down. I avoid the base gym now because that’s where some of us used to debrief, and walking past it makes my chest tight.

Lately, thoughts keep coming—images, really—of doors not being locked or gear left behind, even when I know I checked them. I don’t go back to recheck, but I can’t stop replaying it. It's not just about the incident—it’s like my mind fixates on things that didn’t even happen. I’m on edge, but I can’t tell if it’s because of what I can’t remember… or because my own thoughts feel out of sync with reality. I just need to stay sharp. Can’t fall apart now.
D019-D016_h016.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D016_h017.question:
There’s this thing that’s been… sticking in my mind. About a month ago, there was an incident at the hospital—code blue in ICU, a young patient. I was coordinating staff and supplies, and then suddenly, the crash cart hit me when someone pushed it back too fast. Nothing major, just bruises, really. But since then, I keep seeing that moment—like a flash. The sound, the angle of the cart, a nurse shouting. It just pops up, doesn’t ask permission.

I don’t like talking about it. Even thinking about it too closely, I feel this tightness—like I need to shut it down, change the subject in my head. Oddly, I remember the beeping, the shoes of the resident, even the color of a chart—but not who pulled the crash cart first. That part’s just… missing.

And lately, these thoughts—like, what if I messed up triage that day? What if I didn’t relay something right? I keep replaying it, not because I want to, but because it feels like I *have* to. I haven’t done anything specific to stop them—no rituals or anything. I just push harder at work. But they’re always there, like background noise, tied to *that* moment… I think.
D019-D016_h017.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D019-D016_h017.answer: B & A. Acute Stress Disorder & Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

D019-D016_h018.question:
I’ve been off ever since that accident on set three weeks ago—the one where the lighting rig came down during the live session. I wasn’t hurt, but… I keep hearing the sound of metal twisting right before it gave way. Like a feedback loop in my head. It plays at random, and suddenly I’m sweating, heart jackhammering—I can’t control it. Sometimes I’ll be fiddling with a mixing board and a certain pitch or sudden high frequency will trigger it, and I have to step outside. But I don’t like talking about what happened—whenever someone asks, I shut down. I remember the music playing, the way the lights flickered, but the actual moment? Nothing. Just a blank. There are other bits I can’t place either, like where the stage manager was standing—one second he’s there, next, gone.

Lately, I keep getting these thoughts—random, loud ideas that pop up, like someone else is speaking in my head. Not about the accident, just… nonsense that won’t leave. I’ll hear myself saying, *What if you left the studio door open? What if you didn’t check the cables?* Even after I’ve checked them. I don’t really act on it, but the thoughts stick. I don’t know if it’s stress, or if I’m starting to crack. It’s not constant, but it’s enough to make me second-guess everything.
D019-D016_h018.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D019-D016_h019.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—almost every night now—where I’m back in that ER waiting room, hearing the same sounds, seeing the same faces, but then it shifts, like the lights dim or someone calls my name and I can’t move. I’ve started checking things more than once, but not because I want to—it’s like if I don’t, my mind just gets louder.  

I don’t know if it’s the trauma or just anxiety piling on. Some days I feel okay, others I’m just… stuck.
D019-D016_h019.options:

    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D019-D016_h020.question:
I’ve been struggling ever since that night in the courthouse parking garage—something happened, I know it did, but I can’t remember most of it. It’s like there’s a black hole in my head. I walk past that area now and my chest tightens, my hands go numb. I avoid that entrance entirely, even if it means going up three flights of stairs. Did I imagine it?* It’s not that I *want* to check—it just keeps coming, over and over. I don’t do anything about it, no rituals, nothing like that. But the thoughts won’t leave. I used to sleep through the week. Now I lie awake, exhausted, trying not to think, trying not to remember. It’s been a few weeks—too long to shake it, but I keep thinking it’ll pass. I just need to work through it.
D019-D016_h020.options:
A. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    B. Acute Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D019-D016_h021.question:
I’ve been having these moments—like a wave comes over me, and suddenly I’m back there. Not fully, but enough that I can see his face, hear the voice. It only lasts a few seconds, maybe a minute, but I’ll be working with the wax for a pendant and just… freeze. My hands keep moving, but I’m not here. My assistant had to snap me back once when I nearly burned myself.

I don’t know what’s gotten into me lately. Last week, after one of those episodes, I shoved a client’s sketch across the table. She startled, and I did too—glass pen shattered. I didn’t mean to, but something just boiled over. It’s not like me. I’ve always been private, controlled, but now there are these thoughts—sharp, looping. Not about the past, not exactly, but just... *what if I dropped this piece? What if I ruined everything?* They don’t make sense. I go over details again and again—did I lock the studio? Did I send the invoice? I check once, twice… sometimes more.

It’s been six weeks—since the break-in at the shop. I wasn’t hurt, but they wrecked everything. My work, my tools. I keep thinking: why didn’t I install better locks? I replay it, but the thoughts aren’t tied to that night, not clearly. And the anger—where’s it coming from?
